# LazyMatrix

> LazyMatrix provides Rust and Python interfaces for centering and scaling matrices without materializing them.

The website contains the user guide, benchmark comparisons, and Python and Rust
API references. The Rust API is also hosted on docs.rs. LazyMatrix is in early development, and breaking
changes are expected.

## Documentation

- [What is LazyMatrix?](https://lazymatrix.org/guide/what-is-lazymatrix): An introduction to lazy normalization, supported matrix libraries, and where to go next.
- [Getting started](https://lazymatrix.org/guide/getting-started): Install LazyMatrix in Rust or Python, multiply by a normalized matrix, and reuse fitted parameters.
- [Backend setup](https://lazymatrix.org/guide/installation): Backend features, compiler requirements, optional BLAS acceleration, and Python installation.
- [Normalization](https://lazymatrix.org/guide/normalization): Centering and scaling, column and row recipes, fitted parameter reuse, persistence, and ordered stages.
- [Using normalized matrices](https://lazymatrix.org/guide/matrix-operations): Forward and transpose products, SciPy solvers, submatrices, eager conversion, allocation control, and PyTorch integration.
- [How it works](https://lazymatrix.org/guide/how-it-works): Normalization identities and sparse storage behavior.
- [Python API reference](https://lazymatrix.org/reference/python/): Public classes and methods.
- [Rust API reference](https://lazymatrix.org/reference/rust/): Public types, traits, and methods.
- [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/lazymatrix): The Rust API reference hosted by docs.rs.
- [Benchmarks](https://lazymatrix.org/benchmarks): Construction, repeated operations, and memory costs.
- [Source code](https://github.com/jolars/lazymatrix): Implementation, examples, and releases.

## Development

- [Contributing](https://lazymatrix.org/development/contributing): Reporting bugs, setting up a checkout, checking changes, and opening pull requests.
- [Changelog](https://lazymatrix.org/development/changelog): Rust release notes and breaking changes, with a link to the Python changelog.
